name: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
summary: A coalition of Christian Iberian kings under Alfonso VIII of Castile, supported by Peter II of Aragon, Sancho VII of Navarre, and contingents from Portugal, defeats the Almohad Caliph al-Nasir at a mountain pass north of Jaén. The battle is declared a crusade by Pope Innocent III. The Almohad army, estimated at 120,000 (likely exaggerated), is routed; al-Nasir flees, and according to legend, King Sancho of Navarre breaks through the iron chain guarding the Caliph's tent.

_quarry.structural_significance: The decisive turning point of the Reconquista: within 40 years Córdoba (1236), Valencia (1238), and Seville (1248) fall to Christian kingdoms; the Almohads never recover military dominance in Iberia; Muslim political control retreats to the Emirate of Granada until 1492
